title: Concrete supported common finite-field scalar models and their compatibility predicate
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and the normed algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with finite-subextension-valued coefficient $C$, full continuous coefficient $B$ and their actual inclusion [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For finite intermediate fields $E,F$, define $E_0=E\vee F$ with its existing finite-dimensional instance. Given $E\subseteq A$ finite and a module $L$ on a locally closed support $a:S\hookrightarrow X$, define ordinary scalar extension $L_0$, $K=(a_!L_0)[0]$, and $G=a_!(C\otimes^L_E L[0])$ using the canonical internal scalar/support data [def-sfb-normalized-internal-support-scalars]. Given invertibility of the specified single comparison and normalized support comparisons, define the finite-field reassociations and $\alpha:G\simeq C\otimes^L_AK$, $\alpha_B:JG\simeq B\otimes^L_AK$, and the direct B-support comparison as actual composites, not arbitrary choices. ModelAssertions is the predicate that $L_0$ is lisse [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], $K$ is bounded constant-model constructible [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the single comparison is invertible, these normalized support data exist, $\alpha_B$ equals the direct B comparison, the scalar-unit equation holds after A restriction, and successive units agree with the direct unit. It also includes transport through the fixed underlying-sheaf-preserving section-module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], its specified scalar adjunction [def-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction-data], actual open/closed support operations [def-sfb-section-module-operations], and normalized derived tensors and internal Homs including evaluation [def-sfb-internal-section-total-comparison]. No existence of ModelAssertions is asserted by this definition. The canonical coefficient inclusions are [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map], [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-to-qlbar] and [def-sfb-algcl-topology-inclusion]. The section support comparison is the composite of localization of lowerComparison on the closure and openComparison on its open factor. Use the fixed scalar transpose comparison [def-sfb-open-internal-scalar-transport-data] and its section scalar pair [def-sfb-scalar-hom-comparison-data]. Assemble section alpha independently by finite-field reassociation, the inverse transported normalized support square and the support-single comparison. Assemble section alpha_B by applying the section C-to-B functor and the transported canonical scalar tower. Require their comparison identities with the images of alpha and alpha_B, and the displayed section-unit equation with the actual section scalar unit and the image of the coefficient-induced map. Tensor and Hom preservation use [def-sfb-internal-section-derived-tensor-comparison], [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] and the native braiding [def-sfb-native-derived-koszul-braiding]. Exactness of section open and closed operations is the property transported by [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport].
